subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration — SDK, function calling, streaming, embeddings
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration — SDK, function calling, streaming, embeddings

Hi Alice/Bob — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency-sensitive customer support search and summarization (95th p50 SLA target ~200ms for search + answer).
- High token cost on current hosted LLM provider; need better cost predictability for peak traffic.
- Strict security controls: VPC, KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Replace current generation pipeline for customer-facing responses with a streaming-enabled inference flow to improve perceived latency.
2) Use embeddings + reranking for semantic search to reduce top-K model calls and cost.
3) Maintain structured outputs for downstream ingestion (JSON schema via function calling / structured output enforcement).

Product fit & integration notes from our call:
- SDK: We recommend using Redwood SDK v0.9+ which includes streaming helpers and built-in retry/backoff. Minor repo change: switch from synchronous to streaming client and add on_chunk handlers.
- Function calling: Use function calling for structured outputs (order: call -> parse JSON -> validate schema). We can ship a sample schema for your support ticket payload.
- Streaming: Prefix/KV caching will significantly reduce repeated prefix costs for multi-turn context in chat. We discussed continuous batching for background requests vs. low-latency foreground routing.
- Embeddings & reranking: Pipeline: user query -> vector search (approx nearest neighbors) -> rerank top 10 with lightweight model/ensemble -> final generation only for top candidate(s). This should cut generation token spend by ~60% depending on your rerank thresholds.

Attachments: attached SDK integration guide and draft proposal (redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf, redwood-proposal-acme-2027.pdf). Also linking the HubSpot opportunity and the sample schema in Drive.

Proposed next steps (action owners & target dates):
- Marissa: Share SDK snippet + sample schema and a 30-min technical follow-up with your eng team (target: Thu 22 Apr).
- Rishi: Provide SOC2/Security pack and network topology notes for VPC deployment (target: Fri 23 Apr).
- Alice/Bob: Share a short prioritized list of 3 representative flows and an internal contact for the engineering deep-dive.

If that looks right, I’ll send calendar invites for the technical follow-up.

Thanks again,

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration — SDK, function calling, streaming, embeddings

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of quick clarifications: 
1) For the latency target, the 200ms is for the user-facing answer after we do the rerank; internal search can be a bit higher. Is the streaming approach compatible with the current CDN edge caching we use for static assets?
2) We’ll need SOC2 + any encryption/KMS docs for procurement — appreciate Rishi taking point.

We can do the technical follow-up on Thu 22 Apr at 10:00 PT. I’ll invite our lead platform engineer, Bob Lee.

On flows, I’ll share 3 representative requests (search + summarization, triage classifier, and a short multi-turn support workflow) by EOD tomorrow.

Appreciate the clear next steps — looking forward to the SDK snippet and schema.

Best,
Alice

- SDK snippet: I’ll paste a minimal streaming example in the follow-up thread. For now, note that the streaming client requires a small proto change: your on_chunk handler should assemble partial JSON safely and validate via schema once complete.
